name: Tomato Fruit Bacterial Canker
symptoms: seedlings: No symptoms in most cases Young plants may show poor growth or temporary branch wilting mature_plants_systemic: Curling, yellowing, wilting, and browning (firing) of oldest leaflets Stunted growth and general plant wilting Yellow to reddish-brown pith with mealy appearance Stem streaks, branch breakage, and potential plant death mature_plants_secondary: Dark brown to almost black lesions on leaf margins Round or irregular leaf spotting Fruit: yellow to brown raised spots with persistent white halo ('bird's eye' spots), ~3 mm in diameter Vascular tissue under calyx may be discolored, affecting seeds
management: prevention: Use disease-free seeds and transplants Plant certified clean transplants Strict monitoring of seed fields; discard contaminated lots Soak seed in 130°F water for 25 minutes greenhouse_measures: Steam potting mix and flats Disinfect benches, flats, and irrigation hoses Empty greenhouses between crops field_measures: Avoid working when foliage is wet Incorporate all plant tissue at season's end Rotate fields out of tomato for at least one year Control related weeds around fields chemical_control: Repeated copper applications may reduce disease spread but are not fully reliable Surface disinfectants: bleach (0.5–1% calcium or sodium hypochlorite), Physan, etc.
